source.title: Overfreezing Meets Overparameterization: A Double Descent Perspective on Transfer Learning of Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Yehuda Dar; L. Luzi; Richard Baraniuk

record.tranche_reason: The study measures test-error curves and interpolation in transfer learning, extending double-descent experiments to pretrained and partially frozen networks rather than explicitly reproducing the original from-scratch study.
record.gate_note: The reported epoch-wise and freezing-wise test-error curves bear on the claim. Source-dataset size results are included where the text explicitly reports a delayed or reduced double-descent peak. Exact curve values and some curve-specific dataset sizes are available only in figures. The study also discusses task similarity and training speed; those results do not measure a claim version and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures test-error curves in a new setting: transfer learning of ResNet-18, DenseNet-121 and ViT. It covers epoch-wise double descent and a new freezing-wise double descent, where the number of learnable parameters is varied by freezing layers, each read against the training-error interpolation threshold. It also varies label noise and source and target dataset sizes. It is not one of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. In transfer learning, epoch-wise double descent is more significant for sufficiently large, noisy target datasets and is less likely in few-shot settings. Label noise is crucial for ResNet but not for DenseNet or ViT. Larger source datasets act as implicit regularization, slowing interpolation and sometimes reducing the peak. Freezing many layers can eliminate epoch-wise double descent, and varying the freezing level can produce freezing-wise double descent. Double descent can make transfer from a less related task as good or better.
record.recipe_differences: Uses test classification error and interpolation in deep networks, but studies transfer learning rather than the original from-scratch settings; it varies source and target data sizes and frozen-layer levels instead of conducting the original model-width sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior depends on target dataset size and label noise, architecture, source dataset size, and number of frozen layers. The text also says freezing-wise double descent depends on sufficient resolution in the freezing-level grid and sufficiently long training.

fits_no_version.finding: A larger source dataset slows the target model's arrival at interpolation and delays the double-descent peak. This is strong in ResNet and weaker in DenseNet and ViT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining size acts as implicit regularization that shifts the epoch-wise interpolation threshold and peak later.

fits_no_version.finding: Because of double descent, transfer from a less related source task can match or beat transfer from a more related one for large targets (Figs. 7, E.1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Double-descent peaks can invert the expected benefit of source-target similarity in transfer learning.

record.problems: The relevant test-error outcomes are presented mainly as plots without numerical values or stated uncertainty estimates. Some reported conditions are described only as sufficiently large or as examples, limiting precise comparison across settings.
record.rows_left_out: No further claim-version test results were omitted. The study's task-similarity comparisons and source-size effects on training speed are not separately cataloged where they do not state a test-error-curve outcome bearing on a version.

untested.parts: No width or depth sweep of the architecture. Capacity is varied only through freezing transferred layers.
Training from scratch is shown only as a comparator. Transfer settings only.
No result that more target samples raise test error near the threshold. Larger targets make the peak more likely, but non-monotonicity in sample count is not reported.
Only deep networks are tested; other model classes are not.
No single complexity measure is tested for predicting peak location. The authors only interpret source size as reducing 'effective complexity'.
Multiple or triple peaks, variance as a driver, and optimally tuned explicit regularization are not tested.
There is no recounting of effective parameters.

missing.what: Transfer learning from a small noisy target dataset shows no epoch-wise double descent, while from-scratch training on the same data does (the transfer arm of R7).
Food-101 ResNet without added noise shows double descent, which the authors attribute to inherent label noise.
DenseNet and ViT on CIFAR-10 show a test-error rise at interpolation with no clear second descent.
Additional ViT freezing-wise double-descent panels, and the small-target case (Fig. 6a) where the best freezing level is at interpolation.
missing.locator: Section 4.3 Fig. 6a; Appendix D.2 Figs. D.4, D.5

record.verdict_notes: All outcomes are figure-only, with no numbers or uncertainty. R11-R13 are linked to V1/V4 because freezing changes the learnable-parameter count, not the architecture size; researchers may judge this axis analogous rather than identical to model-wise sweeps. The authors define double descent loosely (footnote 2: a peak at interpolation, without requiring a first descent). The 'effective complexity' language about source size is interpretation, not a test of V5.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or width tests test error as model size grows.
The tests concern training epochs in transfer learning, not a general test of epoch-wise double descent across all deep-network training settings.
Target dataset sizes are varied, but the study does not report that increasing sample size near the interpolation threshold raises test error.
The capacity-like sweep is over frozen-layer levels in DNNs; other model classes and a general capacity sweep are not tested.
The study discusses effective parameterization but does not test whether one measure predicts peak location across size, epochs, and samples.
The study examines label-noise dependence and effects of freezing, but does not test variance as a driver, multiple or triple peaks, or disappearance under optimally tuned regularization.
No re-counting of complexity as an effective parameter number or test of whether that makes the curve an ordinary U-shape.
